stem:
Soham traces a path on square-grid paper. One segment runs $3$ straight grid units along the lines; the next segment cuts diagonally across one square.

Which claim about the path length is correct?

options.text: Call the answer grid path only, without separating straight and diagonal lengths.
Count the diagonal cut as $1$ grid unit, the same as a straight side, with no separate estimate.
Measure the straight parts in grid units and treat the diagonal as longer than one straight grid unit, then add the lengths.
Say that calling the diagonal longer is what creates the grid path itself.

teacher.key_rationale: Straight grid steps and a diagonal cut across a square are not the same unit length, so the diagonal must be measured or estimated separately before adding. Naming only grid path, treating the diagonal as one straight unit, or reversing length and path all miss that distinction.
